prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1148; do not mention it.)
text:
This letter is to advise that our firm now represents the injured party in connection with the collision described in your file. Our client sustained injuries in a low-speed head-on collision and is currently receiving medical care for those injuries. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, either by telephone or in writing.

We request that you disclose the bodily injury liability limits under the policy that covers the at-fault driver, along with a copy of the declarations page confirming those limits and any other coverage that may apply. Please also confirm whether any excess or umbrella coverage exists.

We further ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to this loss. This includes the claim file, photographs, vehicle data and event recorder information, repair or total-loss estimates, recorded statements, telephone logs, and any correspondence with the other driver or third parties. Please suspend any routine destruction of these materials while the claim remains open.

We look forward to your prompt written response confirming receipt of this letter and the requested information.
